Department Information

California’s Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) brings together the state’s recycling and waste management programs to move the state towards a circular economy that reduces waste and reuses all materials.

Through landmark initiatives like the Integrated Waste Management Act and Beverage Container Recycling and Litter Reduction Act, California works toward a society that uses less, recycles more, and takes resource conservation to higher and higher levels.

CalRecycle’s Mission: Protecting California’s environment and climate for the health and prosperity of future generations through the reduction, reuse and recycling of California resources, environmental education, disaster recovery and the transition from a disposable to a fully circular economy.

CalRecycle values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect the environment and preserve resources by empowering Californians to reduce, reuse, and recycle. Join CalRecycle to improve the lives of all Californians.

Department Website: http://www.calrecycle.ca.gov

Job Description And Duties

Do you have a passion to perform a variety of scientific, analytical, and technical assistance duties to implement enforcement requirements and assist with program analysis of compliance policies for Product Stewardship Compliance Branch? Do you enjoy working in a collaborative, dynamic environment? CalRecycle is seeking an enthusiastic Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to join our talented team that is passionate to work in the Product Stewardship Compliance programs!

Position Description:

Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager II (Supervisory) (EPM II) in the Product Stewardship Compliance Branch, the Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) will act as a lead technical expert on the product stewardship compliance programs. The incumbent performs difficult, complex, sensitive scientific and technical duties related to CalRecycle’s product stewardship compliance, including environmental and materials management research, analyses, investigations, and enforcement. The incumbent utilizes principles of scientific research, physical and environmental sciences, and statistical analysis, along with expertise in integrated waste management, industry economics, public health, and resource management. Responsibilities include assessing and enforcing regulations, reviewing and analyzing technical documents, evaluating operations and monitoring records, and conducting inspections and compliance assessments. The incumbent is responsible for determining the significance of violations and their general effect on public health, safety, environmental justice, and the environment for the program. Key duties include providing training and mentoring of staff in the determination of compliance with state minimum standards, offering technical expertise on evaluation and enforcement matters; reviewing findings and reports for technical adequacy; and ensuring that enforcement information in the Department’s databases has been accurately input by staff. Additional duties include process development, monitoring, and evaluation to support various functions of the branch. The incumbent will independently identify problems, develop courses of action, and conduct investigations and studies that yield information and recommendations to improve the department’s oversight of product stewardship compliance programs. Additionally, the incumbent will play a key role in the development and implementation of new enforcement programs related to products with extended producer responsibility (EPR) and product stewardship requirements.

This position involves traveling throughout California involving multiple, consecutive days away from the office and overnight stays. The incumbent must have a current California Driver’s License and participate in the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Employer Pull Notice Program.

This position is required to be in office a minimum of four days per week. This position may be eligible for one day a week telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist – Contaminated Land
jobs.description:
$85,000+ Super + Paid Overtime / TOIL

Large-scale contaminated land investigations

Clear pathway towards Project Management

As an Environmental Scientist in Contaminated Land
, join a growing consultancy at a useful point in your career: you’re beyond graduate level, but you’re not expected to arrive as a finished Project Manager.

With around 2–3 years’ experience, you’ll sit between the junior team and experienced PMs. You’ll stay hands-on with fieldwork and reporting while gradually taking greater ownership of projects as your capability develops.

The project pipeline is getting bigger too. Current and recent work includes a 5-hectare industrial DSI covering soil, groundwater, vapour and surface water, an $800M+ renewable energy project, plus larger infrastructure projects and Tier 1 opportunities currently being tendered.

The Role

Around 2 days per week will typically be in the field, with the balance across reporting and project delivery.

You’ll:

Deliver PSI, DSI, validation and Acid Sulfate Soil investigations.
Undertake soil and groundwater sampling and environmental fieldwork.
Write technical reports with experienced senior review and support.
Build further exposure to RAPs and waste classifications.
Work across commercial, industrial, infrastructure and renewable energy projects.
Gradually take ownership of pieces of work and smaller projects as you develop.

Most fieldwork is around Sydney, Newcastle and surrounding areas, with no expectation of constant overnight or regional travel. Where practical, you can travel directly from home to site.

The Team

This is a small, growing consultancy where you’ll have experienced contaminated land people above you and junior consultants coming through underneath.

They want someone who can take a brief and get moving - not someone who needs every step mapped out. You don’t need to know everything, but you should be willing to research, ask questions and have a crack.

There’s genuine investment in development too. The business supports industry training, professional accreditations and ALGA involvement, including access to specialist technical training in areas such as Acid Sulfate Soils.

Hybrid working is available, alongside company vehicles, fuel cards, PPE, field equipment, laptop and phone. Overtime is paid, TOIL is available and there’s no regular weekend work.

Experience

Around 2–3 years’ environmental consulting experience.
Contaminated land experience across PSI/DSI, sampling and reporting.
Exposure to groundwater, Acid Sulfate Soils and validation; RAP or waste classification experience is useful.
Initiative and an appetite to take on more responsibility.

Salary starts from $85,000 + super, with paid overtime / TOIL.

jobs.description:
Join a consultancy at ground level and help shape its future from day one.

$100,000 - $120,000 + Super | Flexible office hours and genuine autonomy.

Massive $3B Wind Farm, Councils & Contractor projects already secured.

Some consultancies spend years trying to win meaningful work.
This one has spent its first 12 months trying to keep up with it.

Already delivering Contaminated Land projects on a $3B Wind Farm alongside a growing portfolio of Council, contractor and development clients, they're turning work away because there simply aren't enough experienced people to deliver it.

That's where you come in.

Joining as the second senior technical person in the business, you'll immediately step into a Project Management role, taking pressure off the Director while helping shape the systems, culture and direction of a consultancy that's only just getting started.

The exciting part? Very few people get the chance to influence a business this early in its journey.

The Role

You'll lead contaminated land projects from investigation through to reporting while mentoring two graduates who are eager to learn.

Typical work includes:

Preliminary & Detailed Site Investigations (PSI / DSI)Managing contaminated land investigations and reporting
Coordinating field programs, subcontractors and laboratory outputs
Client liaison across Councils, contractors and developersMentoring graduate consultants through fieldwork and reporting
Supporting quality systems as the business continues to grow
Working across major renewables, infrastructure and industrial projects throughout NSW

Over the next 12 months the business is expanding further into contractor support, environmental management plans and broader contaminated land services, so the variety of work will only continue to grow.

The Team

You'll join a close-knit team of four consisting of the Director, two graduates and an office administrator.

It's a genuine start-up environment.

No layers of management.
No politics.
No waiting six months for approval to improve something.

If you've ever wanted to help build a consultancy instead of simply working for one, this is your opportunity.

The Director has deliberately brought in experienced external technical specialists to continue developing both the business and its people, meaning you'll have access to high-level mentoring while also having genuine influence over how the company evolves.

The office is based in the Morisset area with flexibility around office days and working hours.

Experience managing PSI & DSI projectsComfortable running projects with minimal supervision
Strong client communication and report writing skills

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist 5
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Check out this video and find out why our team loves to work here!

Join Us! CDM Smith – where amazing career journeys unfold.

Imagine a place committed to offering an unmatched employee experience. Where you work on projects that are meaningful to you. Where you play an active part in shaping your career journey. Where your co-workers are invested in you and your success. Where you are encouraged and supported to do your very best and given the tools and resources to do so. Where it’s a priority that the company takes good care of you and your family.

Our employees are the heart of our company. As an employer of choice, our goal is to provide a challenging, progressive and inclusive work environment which fosters personal leadership, career growth and development for every employee. We value passionate individuals who challenge the norm, deliver world-class solutions and bring diverse perspectives. Join our team, and together we will make a difference and change the world.

Job Description

We are seeking an Environmental Scientist/Environmental Risk Assessor to support Human Health and Ecological projects for the Environmental Services Group. This candidate will primarily assist with regulatory compliance efforts for federal, state, and local environmental projects in CDM Smith’s portfolio.

Roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

With general direction, supports site investigations and basic to high complexity analysis and interpretation of site data relevant to human health risk assessments (HHRAs) and ecological risk assessments (ERAs).
Supports human health and ecological risk teams and contributes to the process of project tasks, including development of data quality objectives (DQOs), Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), and sampling and analysis plans (SAPs).
With general direction, supports planning for and preparation of conceptual site exposure models (CSEMs), Human Health Risk Assessments (HHRAs), Screening Level Ecological Risk Assessments (SLERAs), and Baseline Ecological Risk Assessments (BERAs) of basic to high complexity.
Collaborates with scientists, geologists, engineers, and toxicologists to provide advice and expertise on the selected project approach, and to implement the approved approach (e.g., investigation, remediation, etc.).
On oversight projects, provides technical evaluation of responsible party’s project documents and supports technical meetings with clients and responsible parties.
Provides technical guidance and training to more junior staff and mentors them for future growth within the discipline and firm.
Collaborates with sales staff to support proposals in response to current and potential client requests for proposal (RFPs).
Contributes to firm's technical knowledge by developing white papers on emerging environmental issues.
Attends and presents at conferences, symposia, and other scientific venues to improve the visibility of the firm's products and services in collaboration with applicable sales staff.
Performs other duties as required.

Skills & Abilities

Expert Knowledge of standard field protocols for their respective discipline.
Expert knowledge of scientific methods and processes.
Expert Knowledge of Microsoft business software (excel, word, etc.).
Excellent verbal and written communications skills.
Expert knowledge of regulations (federal, state, and local) governing environmental review and project implementation.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Science or related discipline with professional scientist registration/certification OR Master's degree in Science or related discipline.
7 years of related experience.
Domestic and/or international travel may be required. The frequency of travel is contingent on specific duties, responsibilities, and the essential functions of the position, which may vary depending on workload and project demands.
Equivalent additional directly related experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in toxicology, environmental science, chemistry, public health, or related disciplines desired with a minimum of seven years of experience in environmental consulting, regulation or a similar environmental field.
Experience with various contaminant classes including (but not limited to) volatile organic compounds (VOCs), metals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), radionuclides, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
Experience with software/digital tools including (but not limited to) the Integrated Exposure Uptake Biokinetic (IEUBK) model, adult lead methodology (ALM) model; U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Regional Screening Level (RSL), Vapor Intrusion Screening Level (VISL), and Radionuclide Preliminary Remediation Goal (PRG) calculator tools; Biotic Ligand Model; Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) EcoRisk database, etc.
Familiarity with Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study (RI/FS) requirements and guidance under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), as well as other state-based programs (e.g., California Department of Toxic Substances Control [DTSC], District Department of the Environment [DDOE]).
Experience supporting clients directly in meetings resolving issues with responsible parties
Experience specific to contaminated sediment sites is desired.

Amount Of Travel Required

10% or less

jobs.title: Geologist/Environmental Scientist - Lake Jackson, TX
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

There will not be any relocation funding provided or negotiated with this position.

As a geologist/environmental scientist you will work alongside a multi-disciplinary team consisting of experienced technicians, engineers, geologists, environmental scientists, and other consulting staff. You will support the delivery of environmental projects by conducting field work, participating in daily tailgate meetings and periodic project-specific calls, reviewing/ evaluating data, reporting, and developing strong relationships with internal staff and clients.

The fieldwork will consist of sampling of various mediums (soil, groundwater, air, concrete, sand-blast media, etc.), environmental/ geotechnical drilling activities, site assessments, oversight of subcontractors, as well as coordinating and planning the aforementioned tasks.

You’ll have the opportunity to help create a more sustainable world by implementing thoughtful environmental practices and procedures while working on an array of diverse projects primarily, but not exclusively, around Freeport, Texas and the greater Houston area. In this role, you’ll be mentored by experienced staff who will help you start your environmental consulting career at a place like no other.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in geology or environmental sciences
Minimum 4 years of experience within environmental consulting or comparable field
Dedication to a robust health and safety culture
Conduct work under minimal supervision and be able to work with a team
Ability to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with a positive attitude
Demonstrate proficiency and ownership in the project tasks  
Willingness and ability to travel up to 70% of the time may be required
Attend tailgate meetings at 7am on Monday through Thursday in Freeport, Texas

Ideally, you will also have

4-6 years of experience within environmental consulting or comparable field
Geology degree or environmental sciences with environmental coursework
Experience working on active project sites and overseeing subcontractors

$85,000+ Super + Paid Overtime / TOIL

Large-scale contaminated land investigations

Clear pathway towards Project Management

As an Environmental Scientist in Contaminated Land
, join a growing consultancy at a useful point in your career: you’re beyond graduate level, but you’re not expected to arrive as a finished Project Manager.

With around 2–3 years’ experience, you’ll sit between the junior team and experienced PMs. You’ll stay hands-on with fieldwork and reporting while gradually taking greater ownership of projects as your capability develops.

The project pipeline is getting bigger too. Current and recent work includes a 5-hectare industrial DSI covering soil, groundwater, vapour and surface water, an $800M+ renewable energy project, plus larger infrastructure projects and Tier 1 opportunities currently being tendered.

The Role

Around 2 days per week will typically be in the field, with the balance across reporting and project delivery.

You’ll:

Deliver PSI, DSI, validation and Acid Sulfate Soil investigations.
Undertake soil and groundwater sampling and environmental fieldwork.
Write technical reports with experienced senior review and support.
Build further exposure to RAPs and waste classifications.
Work across commercial, industrial, infrastructure and renewable energy projects.
Gradually take ownership of pieces of work and smaller projects as you develop.

Most fieldwork is around Sydney, Newcastle and surrounding areas, with no expectation of constant overnight or regional travel. Where practical, you can travel directly from home to site.

The Team

This is a small, growing consultancy where you’ll have experienced contaminated land people above you and junior consultants coming through underneath.

They want someone who can take a brief and get moving - not someone who needs every step mapped out. You don’t need to know everything, but you should be willing to research, ask questions and have a crack.

There’s genuine investment in development too. The business supports industry training, professional accreditations and ALGA involvement, including access to specialist technical training in areas such as Acid Sulfate Soils.

Hybrid working is available, alongside company vehicles, fuel cards, PPE, field equipment, laptop and phone. Overtime is paid, TOIL is available and there’s no regular weekend work.

Experience

Around 2–3 years’ environmental consulting experience.
Contaminated land experience across PSI/DSI, sampling and reporting.
Exposure to groundwater, Acid Sulfate Soils and validation; RAP or waste classification experience is useful.
Initiative and an appetite to take on more responsibility.

Salary starts from $85,000 + super, with paid overtime / TOIL.

Company Overview

Check out this video and find out why our team loves to work here!

Join Us! CDM Smith – where amazing career journeys unfold.

Imagine a place committed to offering an unmatched employee experience. Where you work on projects that are meaningful to you. Where you play an active part in shaping your career journey. Where your co-workers are invested in you and your success. Where you are encouraged and supported to do your very best and given the tools and resources to do so. Where it’s a priority that the company takes good care of you and your family.

Our employees are the heart of our company. As an employer of choice, our goal is to provide a challenging, progressive and inclusive work environment which fosters personal leadership, career growth and development for every employee. We value passionate individuals who challenge the norm, deliver world-class solutions and bring diverse perspectives. Join our team, and together we will make a difference and change the world.

Job Description

We are seeking an Environmental Scientist/Environmental Risk Assessor to support Human Health and Ecological projects for the Environmental Services Group. This candidate will primarily assist with regulatory compliance efforts for federal, state, and local environmental projects in CDM Smith’s portfolio.

Roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

With general direction, supports site investigations and basic to high complexity analysis and interpretation of site data relevant to human health risk assessments (HHRAs) and ecological risk assessments (ERAs).
Supports human health and ecological risk teams and contributes to the process of project tasks, including development of data quality objectives (DQOs), Quality Assurance Project Plans (QAPPs), and sampling and analysis plans (SAPs).
With general direction, supports planning for and preparation of conceptual site exposure models (CSEMs), Human Health Risk Assessments (HHRAs), Screening Level Ecological Risk Assessments (SLERAs), and Baseline Ecological Risk Assessments (BERAs) of basic to high complexity.
Collaborates with scientists, geologists, engineers, and toxicologists to provide advice and expertise on the selected project approach, and to implement the approved approach (e.g., investigation, remediation, etc.).
On oversight projects, provides technical evaluation of responsible party’s project documents and supports technical meetings with clients and responsible parties.
Provides technical guidance and training to more junior staff and mentors them for future growth within the discipline and firm.
Collaborates with sales staff to support proposals in response to current and potential client requests for proposal (RFPs).
Contributes to firm's technical knowledge by developing white papers on emerging environmental issues.
Attends and presents at conferences, symposia, and other scientific venues to improve the visibility of the firm's products and services in collaboration with applicable sales staff.
Performs other duties as required.

Skills & Abilities

Expert Knowledge of standard field protocols for their respective discipline.
Expert knowledge of scientific methods and processes.
Expert Knowledge of Microsoft business software (excel, word, etc.).
Excellent verbal and written communications skills.
Expert knowledge of regulations (federal, state, and local) governing environmental review and project implementation.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Science or related discipline with professional scientist registration/certification OR Master's degree in Science or related discipline.
7 years of related experience.
Domestic and/or international travel may be required. The frequency of travel is contingent on specific duties, responsibilities, and the essential functions of the position, which may vary depending on workload and project demands.
Equivalent additional directly related experience will be considered in lieu of a degree.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in toxicology, environmental science, chemistry, public health, or related disciplines desired with a minimum of seven years of experience in environmental consulting, regulation or a similar environmental field.
Experience with various contaminant classes including (but not limited to) volatile organic compounds (VOCs), metals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), radionuclides, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
Experience with software/digital tools including (but not limited to) the Integrated Exposure Uptake Biokinetic (IEUBK) model, adult lead methodology (ALM) model; U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Regional Screening Level (RSL), Vapor Intrusion Screening Level (VISL), and Radionuclide Preliminary Remediation Goal (PRG) calculator tools; Biotic Ligand Model; Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) EcoRisk database, etc.
Familiarity with Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study (RI/FS) requirements and guidance under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), as well as other state-based programs (e.g., California Department of Toxic Substances Control [DTSC], District Department of the Environment [DDOE]).
Experience supporting clients directly in meetings resolving issues with responsible parties
Experience specific to contaminated sediment sites is desired.

10% or less

new_jobs.title: Geologist/Environmental Scientist - Lake Jackson, TX
new_jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

There will not be any relocation funding provided or negotiated with this position.

As a geologist/environmental scientist you will work alongside a multi-disciplinary team consisting of experienced technicians, engineers, geologists, environmental scientists, and other consulting staff. You will support the delivery of environmental projects by conducting field work, participating in daily tailgate meetings and periodic project-specific calls, reviewing/ evaluating data, reporting, and developing strong relationships with internal staff and clients.

The fieldwork will consist of sampling of various mediums (soil, groundwater, air, concrete, sand-blast media, etc.), environmental/ geotechnical drilling activities, site assessments, oversight of subcontractors, as well as coordinating and planning the aforementioned tasks.

You’ll have the opportunity to help create a more sustainable world by implementing thoughtful environmental practices and procedures while working on an array of diverse projects primarily, but not exclusively, around Freeport, Texas and the greater Houston area. In this role, you’ll be mentored by experienced staff who will help you start your environmental consulting career at a place like no other.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in geology or environmental sciences
Minimum 4 years of experience within environmental consulting or comparable field
Dedication to a robust health and safety culture
Conduct work under minimal supervision and be able to work with a team
Ability to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment with a positive attitude
Demonstrate proficiency and ownership in the project tasks  
Willingness and ability to travel up to 70% of the time may be required
Attend tailgate meetings at 7am on Monday through Thursday in Freeport, Texas

Ideally, you will also have

4-6 years of experience within environmental consulting or comparable field
Geology degree or environmental sciences with environmental coursework
Experience working on active project sites and overseeing subcontractors
Strong attention to detail when conducting field work and evaluating data
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Ability to work closely with clients and demonstrate proficiency when discussing project tasks

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $68,400.00 to $101,000.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on October 26, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

Onsite employees are expected to attend a Jacobs Workplace on a full-time basis, as required by the nature of their role.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.
